svg.aria-label: Animated comparison of FIFO and textbook CLOCK on the access trace A B E A B with four slots and all referenced bits 0. FIFO zaps recently used page A to load E, then refaults A and B, for 3 faults. CLOCK clears the referenced bits of A and B, zaps C instead, and finishes with 1 fault.

g.text: Same trace, 4 slots: FIFO vs textbook CLOCK
A's bit is 1: clear it, skip
B's bit is 1: clear it, skip
Both caches hold the same pages, and a past sweep cleared every bit.
FIFO evicts by age and ignores use: recently used A goes first.
A was used since the hand last passed and gets a second chance.
B gets the same second chance.
C is the first page nobody used.
FIFO pays for throwing out A.
FIFO pays again for throwing out B.
The guest uses A, and FIFO hits without recording anything.
FIFO also hits on B and records nothing.
CLOCK marks B as used, like A before it.
E is in neither cache, and each must evict a page to load it.
FIFO loads E into A's old slot; B is now the oldest.
CLOCK loads E; the hand moves on to D.
FIFO loads A back for its second fault, and C becomes the oldest.
In CLOCK, A is still cached: the hit sets its bit again.
FIFO loads B back, its third fault in this trace.
B is still in the CLOCK cache and hits as well.
Checking recent use kept the hot pages; FIFO threw them out by age.
